program_name: Los Angeles County Measure W (Safe, Clean Water Program)
administering_agency: Los Angeles County Flood Control District / Public Works
statutory_citation: Los Angeles County Flood Control District Code Chapter 16
eligible_improvements: Urban street tree canopy planting with verified 24-hr stormwater runoff capture (min. 85th percentile storm event: 0.75-1.0 in)
Infiltration basins, bio-retention swales, permeable pavers, and curbside rain gardens
Multi-benefit green stormwater infrastructure
how_to_apply: Annual Call for Projects via the Safe, Clean Water Portal; technical and community scoring by Watershed Area Steering Committees

verification.evidence_quote: source https://safecleanwaterla.org/ returned HTTP 403 to every fetch

program_name: City of Los Angeles Proposition K (L.A. for Kids Program)
administering_agency: City of Los Angeles Bureau of Engineering & Department of Recreation and Parks
statutory_citation: City of Los Angeles Ordinance No. 171215
eligible_improvements: Urban greenway development, trail linkages, and community park expansion
Urban tree canopy planting in parklands and public rights-of-way
Recreation facilities and youth athletic field restoration
how_to_apply: Competitive request for proposals (RFP) administered through the Bureau of Engineering

program_name: California Urban Greening Grant Program (Cap-and-Trade GGRF)
eligible_improvements: Street tree planting and urban forest establishment (minimum 20-year maintenance commitment)
Green streets, active transportation greenways, and urban heat island mitigation corridors
Community gardens and urban greening on public parcels
how_to_apply: Annual statewide competitive grant application through CNRA System for Online Application Review (SOAR)

verification.evidence_quote: Public Resources Code section 75114 does not exist in the Legislature's 2025-26 code data (LAW_SECTION_TBL.dat); source resources.ca.gov returned HTTP 403

program_name: CAL FIRE Urban & Community Forestry Grants
administering_agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE)
statutory_citation: Cal. Pub. Res. Code §§ 4799.06-4799.12 (California Urban Forestry Act of 1978; grants at § 4799.12)
eligible_improvements: Urban tree planting, care, and canopy maintenance in urban areas
Urban forest management plans and inventories
Green schoolyards and canopy shade over playgrounds
funding_share_description: Grants of 25 to 90 percent of project costs; the cost share may be waived for projects in disadvantaged and low-income communities (Pub. Res. Code 4799.12). Previous record said 100% / 75%.

verification.evidence_quote: Pub. Res. Code 4799.12: "The director ... may make grants to provide assistance of 25 to 90 percent of costs ... The director may waive the cost sharing requirement for projects that are in disadvantaged and low-income communities."

program_name: Texas Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone (TIRZ / Chapter 311)
administering_agency: Texas Municipalities, Counties, and Local TIRZ Boards
eligible_improvements: Station-area street reconstruction, sidewalk expansion, and utility undergrounding
Protected bicycle lanes and multi-modal transit connector paths
Stormwater detention ponds, green infrastructure, and public open space plazas
funding_share_description: Share of tax increment dedicated to the zone is set by the reinvestment zone financing plan; a taxing unit other than the creating municipality contributes up to 15 percent unless a larger portion is provided (Tax Code 311.013).
how_to_apply: City council or commissioners court petition and ordinance designation pursuant to Tex. Tax Code § 311.005

verification.evidence_quote: Tax Code 311.013: for "a taxing unit other than the municipality that created the zone, a portion, not to exceed 15 percent, of the tax increment produced by the unit as provided by the reinvestment zone financing plan or a larger portion as provided by Subsection (f)"

program_name: Florida Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA Trust Fund)
administering_agency: Local community redevelopment agencies (Fla. Stat. ch. 163, part III)
eligible_improvements: Transit-oriented streetscape improvements, crosswalks, and street lighting
Façade and structural rehabilitation grants for commercial/residential conversions
Public parking structure and greenway connections
funding_share_description: Captures 95% of incremental ad valorem tax revenues from county and city taxing authorities into the CRA redevelopment trust fund
how_to_apply: Application through local municipal CRA office; projects must align with adopted Community Redevelopment Plan

verification.evidence_quote: Fla. Stat. 163.387: increment "shall be ... an amount equal to 95 percent of the difference between" taxes levied each year and taxes levied in the base year
fields_unconfirmed: administering_agency (Department of Economic Opportunity named in earlier record not confirmed)

program_name: Florida Live Local Act 75% Property Tax Exemption
eligible_improvements: Newly constructed or substantially rehabilitated multifamily developments providing at least 40% affordable units (≤120% AMI) for 30 years
funding_share_description: 75% of assessed value exempt for qualifying units at 80-120% of area median income; 100% exemption from ad valorem taxes for units at or below 80% (196.1978(3)(d)). Previous record cited 196.1979, which is a separate local-option exemption.

verification.evidence_quote: Fla. Stat. 196.1978(3)(d)1.a: "The property appraiser shall exempt: a. Seventy-five percent of the assessed value of the units in multifamily projects ... greater than 80 percent but not more than 120 percent of the median annual adjusted gross income"; units at or below 80 percent are exempt from ad valorem taxes

program_name: Colorado Urban Renewal Authority (URA) Tax Increment Financing
administering_agency: Local Colorado Urban Renewal Authorities and Municipalities
eligible_improvements: Transit-oriented community infrastructure, environmental remediation, and multi-modal transit hubs
Utility capacity upgrades to support 40+ units/acre density near passenger rail under HB 24-1313
Public plazas, street trees, and protected pedestrian paths
funding_share_description: Property tax (and optionally municipal sales tax) increment within the urban renewal area may be allocated for up to 25 years under the plan (C.R.S. 31-25-107).
how_to_apply: Urban renewal plan adoption by city council with statutory blight/condition study and taxing entity agreements

verification.evidence_quote: C.R.S. 31-25-107: taxes in the urban renewal area "must be divided for a period not to exceed twenty-five years after the effective date of adoption of such a provision"

program_name: Illinois Transit Tax Increment Financing (Transit TIF)
administering_agency: City of Chicago Department of Planning and Development / Chicago Transit Authority
eligible_improvements: Major passenger rail station modernization, track infrastructure, and Americans with Disabilities Act accessibility
Direct station-adjacent transit-oriented public realm improvements
how_to_apply: Intergovernmental agreement between municipality and transit authority approved by city council

program_name: Arizona Government Property Lease Excise Tax (GPLET Abatement)
administering_agency: Arizona Municipalities (Phoenix, Tucson, Tempe, Mesa) and County Treasurers
eligible_improvements: High-density mixed-use redevelopment and transit-oriented housing in designated central business districts (CBDs) or redevelopment areas
funding_share_description: Cities and towns may abate the government property lease excise tax for up to eight years after the certificate of occupancy for qualifying government property improvements in a single central business district (A.R.S. 42-6209).
how_to_apply: Economic development agreement approved by city council following statutory economic impact analysis

verification.evidence_quote: A.R.S. 42-6209: a city or town "may abate the tax provided for under this article for a limited period beginning when the certificate of occupancy is issued and ending eight years after" in a single central business district
fields_unconfirmed: it abates the government property lease excise tax, not the ad valorem tax, per the text

program_name: Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail Grant Program
administering_agency: Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) / U.S. Department of Transportation
statutory_citation: 49 U.S.C. § 24911 (Federal-State partnership for intercity passenger rail)
eligible_improvements: Capital projects to establish new intercity passenger rail corridors (e.g. Phoenix-Tucson, Austin-San Antonio, Front Range)
High-speed rail guideways, passenger stations, track electrification, and vehicle maintenance facilities (railyards)
Intermodal facilities and station area safety/capacity upgrades
funding_share_description: Federal share may not exceed 80 percent of total project costs, except as specified in paragraph (4) of 49 U.S.C. 24911(f).
how_to_apply: Competitive Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) application submitted via Grants.gov by state DOTs, regional authorities, or multi-state compacts

verification.evidence_quote: 49 U.S.C. 24911: "The Federal share of total costs for a project under this section shall not exceed 80 percent, except as specified under paragraph (4)."
